milestone: Alpha 1.76 persistence compatibility; shared recovery readiness for 1.81/1.82
confirmedPriorBehavior: The legacy helper used mongorestore --drop against an existing target. MongoDB documents that collections absent from an archive are not dropped, so restoring an older snapshot could leave newer operation ledgers alongside older users/schema markers. Existing readiness/stopped-writer guards did not detect that mixed recovery set. No production restore incident is claimed.
changes: Default restores require an empty eidolon target. A non-empty target is refused before writes unless the operator additionally supplies --replace-eidolon-database after --confirm-data-loss. After existing stopped-writer and credential guards, a read-only collection probe and archive dry-run precede any mutation. Explicit replacement drops the fixed eidolon database before namespace-limited archive import, avoiding retained later collections; other databases are not replacement targets. Instructions explain whole-database data loss, incomplete-restore handling, matching journals/server, manual checksum verification and continued admission shutdown. No production restore, automatic archive selection, arbitrary target-name interpolation, writer stop/start, schema change or player-state repair was performed.

proposedPatchNote: Mongo recovery now refuses non-empty targets unless whole-Eidolon replacement is explicitly approved. Archive preflight runs before destructive replacement, preventing older snapshots from silently retaining newer operation collections. Operator recovery instructions clarify matching journals, compatible servers and data-loss risks.
limits: The helper remains an explicitly authorized, destructive Mongo-only recovery, not image rollback or coordinated journal restoration. Dry-run cannot guarantee later BSON/index/IO success; after replacement, a failure can leave all prior Eidolon data gone. Writers must remain stopped until the full recovery set is verified.

Stopped Compose API checks are not a global writer/deployment lock. The owner/operator must stop external writers, serialize recovery and approve the exact archive and loss of subsequent progress; tests do not authorize production use.

Synthetic raw archival fields/ledgers prove retention and replacement boundaries, not business-valid operation replay, full-game startup, majority failover, recovery time objectives or complete 1.76/1.81/1.82 acceptance. Compatible earlier journal/game recovery proofs remain separate; owner backup/retention/RPO/RTO decisions remain open.

Source is local and unpublished; accepted public release remains Alpha1.70.2. No version promotion, push, deployment or whole-roadmap completion is claimed. Earlier recovery-method, jump and data-policy choices and ordered release gates remain open.
